result.question: I'm worried the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at MAIN may be involved. Pull co and co2 for every sample in the available window and work out the CO2/CO ratio for each sample. Flag any sample with a ratio below 3, which suggests paper involved in a fault, or above 10, which suggests general cellulose ageing. Also give me the min, max and mean of co and co2 over the window. Tell me whether the ratio is trending up or down across the samples. If co2 is missing for a sample, skip the ratio for that sample and say so. If co2 has no data at all, report the co trend alongside oxygen instead and say that the ratio test couldn't be done.
result.answer:
All data is in hand — no further calls are needed. `co2` was present and non-null for all 5 samples, so no ratio had to be skipped and the oxygen fallback was not required.

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — CO₂/CO ratio check

**Window:** 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 (5 daily samples, both `co` and `co2` present in every sample)

| Timestamp | CO (ppm) | CO₂ (ppm) | CO₂/CO | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 32 | 1344 | 42.00 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-16 | 30 | 1300 | 43.33 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-17 | 35 | 1350 | 38.57 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-18 | 33 | 1325 | 40.15 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-19 | 32 | 1340 | 41.88 | ⚠ >10 — general cellulose ageing |

- **Samples with ratio < 3 (paper involved in a fault):** none
- **Samples with ratio > 10 (general cellulose ageing):** all 5
- **Samples skipped for missing CO₂:** none

**Window statistics**

| Sensor | Min | Max | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| CO | 30 | 35 | 32.4 |
| CO₂ | 1300 | 1350 | 1331.8 |

**Ratio trend:** Marginally **down** — 42.00 at the first sample to 41.88 at the last, with a least-squares slope of about −0.34 per day. In practice it's essentially flat, oscillating between 38.6 and 43.3 with no sustained direction over 5 samples.

**Interpretation:** Every sample sits well above 10, which is consistent with general/normal cellulose ageing rather than paper being involved in an active thermal or electrical fault (that would show a ratio below 3). The CO and CO₂ levels are also stable across the window with no step change, so there's no sign of an accelerating paper-degradation event. If you want to firm this up, a `interpret_dga` run on the hydrocarbon gases or `predict_health_index` on the full oil-quality set would tell you whether any non-cellulose fault is present alongside this.
